QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_48

question.text: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations 2018, the definition of 'For Profit Social Enterprise' specifically EXCLUDES which type of entity?

answer.text: Partnership firms with more than 20 partners.
Limited Liability Partnerships with foreign LPs.
A company incorporated under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.2.2(B), the ICDR definition of FPE is 'a company or a body corporate operating for profit, which is a social enterprise for the purpose of ICDR Regulations and does not include a company incorporated under Section 8 of the Companies Act 2013.' Section 8 companies are classified as NPOs (per Box 2.2), so the exclusion avoids double-counting. The Trap: Options A, C and D invent unrelated carve-outs that do not exist in ICDR. Cross-Exam Context: III-A / III-C (Compliance) track definitional carve-outs. XII (SMF) treats Companies Act entity taxonomy. Assessor's Pro-Tip: In your engagement scoping, confirm the client's legal form against the FPE/NPO bright line: Section 8 = NPO path (ZCZP), any other for-profit = FPE path (equity/debt). Scoping wrong at this stage invalidates the assurance standard selection (SAS-XX for NPO-side indicators vs FPE-side).
